extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (LEAs, IHEs, other educational entities), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for educational recipients to implement and comply with the Department's 2024 Title IX final regulations, including obligations on grievance procedures, pregnancy-related accommodations, scope of sex discrimination, training, notifications, supportive measures, monitoring, and RIA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation space requirement (§106.40(b)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide an appropriate lactation space for students and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space must be private and clean and not a bathroom; there is no requirement that a lactation space be a particular size, shape, or include features other than being private and clean and not a bathroom. Lactation spaces need not be designated 24 hours a day. Recipients are not required to make particular changes to facilities or provide any precise number of spaces; compliance can generally be achieved using existing space at minimal/de minimis cost. Minimal retrofits (e.g., keypad locks or a chair) are allowable and costs considered de minimis. The Department views these de minimis costs as outweighed by benefits (allowing students/employees to remain in school/work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for pregnancy-related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide reasonable modifications only to students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations require reasonable modifications for the pregnant student; they do not require modifications for partners, family members, or others who are not pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions. The Department did not analyze costs for modifications not imposed by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements (§106.40(b)(2) and (b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and their employees (including Title IX Coordinators) must inform students of their rights under the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost associated with an employee or Title IX Coordinator informing a student of their rights is de minimis and considered part of the Title IX Coordinator's duties. These notification duties are considered alongside training requirements (see §106.40(d)) and are accounted for in the RIA cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to provide abortion-related benefits (§§106.40 and 106.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 106.40 and 106.57(e) do not require recipients to provide or pay for any benefit or service related to abortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters' concerns about abortion-related costs are unfounded; costs raised by commenters are speculative or unrelated to the pregnancy provisions' requirements. See definition discussion for “pregnancy or related conditions” in §106.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sex discrimination (§106.10) — covered categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department clarifies Title IX's scope to include discrimination based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, pregnancy or related conditions, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying scope may result in marginal increases in recipient costs (e.g., investigations), but non-monetary benefits of clarity and fulfilling Title IX's protections justify implementation costs. The Department estimates inclusion may result in a 10 percent increase in investigations annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on different treatment causing more than de minimis harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise permitted by statute/regulation, a recipient must not carry out any otherwise permissible different treatment or separation on the basis of sex in a way that would cause more than de minimis harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes policies or practices that prevent a person from participating in an education program or activity consistent with their gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures requirement — prompt and equitable resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt grievance procedures that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of complaints of sex discrimination and take other necessary steps to provide an educational environment free from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures should be designed to address sex discrimination broadly (not limited to sexual harassment), and recipients may adapt procedures to their size, population, and administrative structure while ensuring equitable treatment of parties. The final regulations revise requirements to allow flexibility but maintain equity. Changes to grievance procedures are a major source of Year 1 costs (policy review, training) but may yield cost savings in subsequent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator monitoring obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators must monitor their education program or activity for barriers to reporting sex discrimination and take steps reasonably calculated to address those barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring and addressing barriers is part of recipients' obligations and factored into benefits (improved reporting, reduced prevalence) and costs (staff time, program changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements (scope and strengthening) (§106.40(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations modify and strengthen training requirements by specifying the range of relevant persons that a recipient must train regarding its obligations under Title IX and the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must cover employee actions required under notification and other provisions; training costs are included in the RIA. The Department anticipates ongoing training costs (Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, other designated personnel) tied to implementation and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory employee notification to Title IX Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notification duties aim to improve reporting and earlier responses; associated time/costs are considered de minimis or captured in training and Title IX Coordinator duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures requirement (§106.44(f)(1)(ii) and (g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination (including harassment and retaliation), the Title IX Coordinator must offer and coordinate supportive measures, as appropriate, to the complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(g) clarifies that for allegations of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment or retaliation, providing supportive measures does not require the recipient or its agents to alter the alleged discriminatory conduct. Supportive measures cover a range of non-disciplinary, non-punitive individualized services; the number of requests for supportive measures may increase and associated costs are included in the Department's model, though many such costs are expected to be small or offset over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide remedies when discrimination determined
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient determines that sex discrimination has occurred, the recipient must provide remedies, as appropriate, to a complainant and any person identified as having their equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must take prompt and effective steps to ensure sex discrimination does not continue or recur. Remedies differ from supportive measures and may include actions to eliminate the discrimination's effects; costs and implementation of remedies are considered in the RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness obligation — respond promptly and effectively regardless of complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44 requires a recipient with knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination in its education program or activity to respond promptly and effectively, regardless of whether a complaint is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an expansion from the 2020 amendments (which focused on reports made to certain employees regarding sexual harassment) and prescribes actions a recipient must take to operate free from sex discrimination. The Department expects improved responsiveness and deterrence, with initial short-term costs expected to be minimal and offset by long-term reductions in discrimination incidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures vs. eliminating source of discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures do not require eliminating the source of the sex discrimination; elimination may be a remedy but is not required as a supportive measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For many forms of discrimination (e.g., unequal access to resources or facilities), few supportive measures are appropriate other than eliminating the discriminatory source, which is treated as a remedy rather than a supportive measure (see §§106.2, 106.44(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs captured in RIA (investigations, adjudications, appeals, monitoring, recordkeeping, supportive measures, training)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department estimates costs associated with implementing the final regulations, including one-time policy/training revisions and ongoing costs for Title IX Coordinators' training, supportive measures, investigations/adjudications, appeals, informal resolutions, recordkeeping, and monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Year 1 costs are higher due to one-time implementation; Years 2–10 show estimated cost savings largely from grievance procedure flexibility. The Department estimates net costs (NPV) and annualized costs at 7% and 3% discount rates and models a 10% increase in investigations annually. Due to data limitations, estimates reflect likely costs but not full quantification of benefits of reduced discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in grievance procedures to reduce burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations allow recipients flexibility to design grievance procedures consistent with Title IX, which the Department expects will reduce administrative burdens and yield cost savings in later years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexibility is expected to increase use of grievance procedures and to contribute to prompt/equitable resolution; the Department models cost savings from this flexibility in Years 2–10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exemptions unchanged (§106.12) and First Amendment protections (§106.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not change §106.12 relating to religious exemptions and explicitly state nothing requires recipients to restrict rights protected under the First Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious institutions are not required to seek assurance before asserting an exemption (may do so voluntarily). The Department does not anticipate an increase in requests for religious exemptions and states that the regulations prohibit sex discrimination (conduct), not require changes to religious beliefs. For further info see Hostile Environment and Religious Exemptions discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of menstruation or related conditions within scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department clarifies that menstruation or related conditions are included within the scope of Title IX as defined in §106.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying inclusion may cause marginal increases in costs for recipients that previously limited policies; however, the regulations do not require recipients to incur the cost of providing menstrual products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) principles for agency rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency must comply with Executive Order 13563 (and 12866) principles: propose/adopt regulations only when benefits justify costs; tailor regulations to impose the least burden consistent with objectives; choose approaches that maximize net benefits; specify performance objectives rather than prescriptive compliance methods where feasible; identify/assess alternatives including non-regulatory incentives; and use best available techniques to quantify anticipated benefits and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states it followed these principles and used available evidence to conclude benefits justify costs. RIA must identify need, costs, benefits, assumptions, limitations, data sources, and alternatives considered; OMB review applies for significant regulatory actions under EO 12866.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for regulatory action — stakeholder input and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department must show need for regulatory action based on statutory directives, case law, enforcement experience, and stakeholder feedback (public hearings, listening sessions, written comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department relied on Executive Orders directing review, extensive stakeholder input (public hearing with 280+ live comments and 30,000+ written comments), and identified gaps/concerns (grievance process burdens, scope of sexual harassment, actual knowledge/deliberate indifference standards, pregnancy protections). The RIA documents that the rule aims to improve fairness and safety and ensure Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate is fully and fairly implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation methodology and baseline establishment for cost/benefit modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: RIA must describe data sources, the model used for estimating costs, assumptions, limitations, and establishment of a baseline of current practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes limited quantitative data on recipients' current practices; it requested data during the NPRM. Due to variation among >24,000 recipients and limited status-quo data (especially LEAs), precise estimates are difficult; nevertheless, the Department provides NPV and annualized cost estimates and explains assumptions and modeling choices throughout the RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of types of sex-based harassment covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination includes sex-based harassment in the form of quid pro quo harassment, hostile environment harassment, and four specific offenses (as clarified by the final regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations clarify the scope of sexual harassment and prescribe recipient obligations for responding; these clarifications are intended to reduce occurrence and facilitate prompt and equitable resolution, even where benefits are not fully quantifiable in monetary terms.
